A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoTEF and MoTEF-VR research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, table, algorithms and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated proofs and renumbered experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic least-squares experiments, logistic-regression evaluations on a9a and w8a, and MLP training results in Section 4 and Figures 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds client-scaling comparisons, spectral-gap experiments, CNN training and CEDAS comparisons, including Figure 7 in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same model updates, compression, error feedback, momentum tracking and STORM estimator. The expanded algorithm explanations and additional evaluation architectures do not change the proposed optimization procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds logistic-regression evaluations on a7a, ijcnn1 and mushrooms beyond the retained a9a/w8a coverage. Appendix D.2 also introduces synthetic evaluations on random regular communication graphs. These substantially broaden datasets and network environments. Naming MNIST for the retained MLP experiment is additional disclosure, not independently established new coverage.

E2.justification: CEDAS, previously included only in theoretical comparisons, becomes an empirical comparator in Appendix D.5/Figure 7. BEER also gains explicit participation in the client-count scaling comparison in Figure 1(a). The existing BEER, Choco-SGD, DSGD and D2 benchmark comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Separate new protocols include noiseless synthetic tests with 400 clients and iterations to error 10^(-3), CNN evaluations using accuracy/loss versus epochs, and CEDAS comparisons with 10 clients, batch size 16 and regularization 0.1. The latter use Rand-K for CEDAS and Top-K for MoTEF, both K=10. These additions do not replace the retained logistic-regression protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a BEER control for the client-scaling analysis and a direct sensitivity study comparing observed spectral-gap dependence with theoretical reference rates. These address linear speedup and the suspected looseness of the network-dependence bound beyond v1's momentum, heterogeneity and logistic-regression topology studies.

E5.justification: Appendix D.5 newly reports averaging the CEDAS comparison over three random seeds; v1 provides no corresponding repeated-run reporting. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests. This addition does not establish an increased run count for retained experiments.

E6.justification: New results show BEER lacking MoTEF's client-scaling behavior, weaker empirical spectral-gap sensitivity than the theoretical bound, and faster CNN convergence for MoTEF. Figure 7 reports similar MoTEF/CEDAS performance on ijcnn1 and mushrooms and a MoTEF advantage on a7a and a9a. These are additional findings under their documented settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: New Appendices B.1.1–B.1.2 derive consensus-error convergence and stationarity of local models beyond the averaged-model analysis. The MoTEF-VR derivation changes two noise-term denominators from n^3 to n^2, revising corresponding network-dependent complexity terms from n^(-1) to n^(-2/3). The shorter MoTEF bounds mainly remove dominated terms. The revision remains internally inconsistent because v2 Equation (45) retains n^3 where Equation (50) uses n^2.

C1.justification: The central claims about optimal stochastic asymptotic scaling, arbitrary heterogeneity and variance reduction remain. Section 3.2 narrows the PL-regime novelty claim from achieving optimal asymptotic complexity to achieving linear speedup in n. The more explicit distributed-SGD comparison in the abstract largely foregrounds a claim already present in v1.

C2.justification: v1 already acknowledged spectral-gap limitations and empirical topology robustness. v2 more explicitly distinguishes stochastic optimality from deterministic spectral-gap suboptimality and discusses whether the latter reflects the method or its analysis. Appendix A.1 also explains the complementary roles of error feedback, gradient tracking and momentum.

D1.justification: v2 adds CNN architecture and tuning details, random-graph degrees and spectral gaps, and compressor choices and parameter grids for the CEDAS comparison. It also identifies MNIST as the dataset for the retained MLP experiment. Existing hardware, repository access and the original logistic-regression tuning information remain materially unchanged.

R1.justification: The new extended related-work appendix substantially compares spectral-gap dependencies across methods and assumptions, including APAPC, ProxSkip and COLD. New lower-bound references support the optimality discussion, and Section 1.1 explicitly acknowledges Takezawa et al.'s earlier momentum tracking without compression. This changes research positioning beyond the switch to numbered citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, algorithm introduction and conclusion are revised, and citations switch to numbered form. The MoTEF-VR Lyapunov lemma and explanation move into Appendix C, with a new related-work appendix and acknowledgement section. Most existing exposition and the overall problem–theory–experiments sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from two to four panels, and new multi-panel CNN and CEDAS figures are added. Existing plots receive revised legends, colors and captions; the MLP plot is enlarged and relocated. The former MLP Figure 4 and topology Figure 5 become Figures 5 and 4 respectively, representing substantial visual reorganization.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens theoretical completeness and empirical support: it connects averaged-model convergence to consensus and local-model stationarity, directly investigates the spectral-gap limitation, and adds documented CNN and CEDAS comparisons. Expanded prior-work attribution also clarifies the contribution. The MoTEF-VR correction yields weaker client-count dependence and is incompletely propagated between Equations (45) and (50), so the theoretical cleanup remains imperfect. Nevertheless, the added guarantees and targeted evidence provide a clear substantial overall improvement.
